brief: bloomCap() is the town’s only STEPPED seasonal term — 3 / 2 / 1 — in a file where growF, dieF, leafCol, riverRun and greyF are all lerps. So the beds’ ripeness falls off a cliff at the autumn shoulder instead of fading: one frame the beds carry three bloom stages, the next they carry two, and every bed in the town steps together. #29’s market carry-over softened what happens downstream; the step itself has never been touched, and it has been the strongest cue open for three manager passes (was c50). Make the ceiling continuous without moving the year’s totals.
successLooksLike: A folded-year probe of bloomCap()’s effective value shows no discontinuity at any phase; the value at SEASON_START is exactly today’s; and the annual mean of blooming cells is within a few percent of a stashed HEAD baseline — the shoulder softened, not the year made warmer.
avoid: A ceiling is not a kill term: do not add a removal term to smooth it — if the cap comes down gradually the beds age out under it by themselves. Bloom stages are integers, so a continuous cap needs per-cell variance (hash(x, y+k)) at the BED’s grain to stop a whole ring stepping in one frame; #25 is the record of what happens when an inherited rule is applied at the wrong grain. And check the shoulder PAIR averages to the anchor, not each shoulder alone.
